question: Summarize how learning curves help diagnose overfitting in the ML diagnostics handbook.
answer: Learning curves help diagnose overfitting by plotting training error and validation error against the training set size [S1]. In a high-variance model, the training error is low and there's a large gap between training error and validation error [S1]. As more data is added, the validation error keeps falling, indicating overfitting [S1]. When a model is overfitting, the first actions to try are a simpler model, stronger regularization, more training data, or early stopping [S1].

citations.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
citations.text:
1. Reading Learning Curves
A learning curve plots training error and validation error against the training set size. In a high-bias
model both errors are high and they converge close to each other; adding more data barely helps
because the model is too simple. In a high-variance model the training error is low and a large gap
separates it from the validation error; the validation error keeps falling as more data is added, so
collecting more data helps.
When a model is overfitting the first actions to try are a simpler model, stronger regularization,
more training data or early stopping.

S2.title: Ml Overfitting Mitigation Guide
S2.text: Overfitting mitigation guide OVERFITTING MITIGATION GUIDE - TracePilot demo course pack (Machine Learning Fundamentals) Original educational material, CC BY 4.0, (c) Faris Mohamed Kishtah. 1. What overfitting means in practice A model overfits when its training accuracy is far higher than its validation accuracy. The gap between the two (train accuracy minus validation accuracy) is the simplest warning sign. 2. L2 regularization (weight decay) L2 regularization adds a penalty proportional to the sum of squared weights to the loss, which shrinks weights toward zero without usually making them exactly zero. Advantages: it is smooth, works with gradient-based optimizers, and keeps all features. Disadvantages: it introduces a strength hyperparameter (lambda or weight decay) that must be tuned with cross-validation, and it does not remove irrelevant features. It

S4.title: Ml Lecture Notes
S4.text: is bias squared plus variance plus irreducible noise. Increasing model complexity lowers bias but raises variance.  Ways to reduce overfitting include collecting more training data, simplifying the model, regularization (L1 and L2 penalties that shrink weights; L1 can drive weights to exactly zero), early stopping, dropout for neural networks, feature selection and cross-validation to choose hyperparameters. Learning curves, which plot error against training set size, help diagnose whether a model suffers from high bias or high variance.
